requirements.system_goal: Deliver a Telegram-first astrology service that authenticates users, captures birth data, sells or grants access, generates structured reports, serves a daily feed, and closes the loop through referrals and bot notifications.

assumptions.assumption: Use-case grouping is inferred from the current route families and service files because the repository does not yet expose a separate canonical capability map.

in_scope.item: Telegram WebApp and bot identity bootstrap, profile onboarding, and profile update.
User-driven report creation from a saved profile with entitlement checks.
Async report generation, section regeneration, report readback, and report-level status tracking.
Payment initiation, webhook processing, subscriptions, credits, and entitlement consumption.
Referral resolution on signup and partner payout on successful payment.
Daily feed generation based on engine facts and optional LLM interpretation.
Admin dashboards, user/client/report operations, broadcasts, and diagnostics trigger.
Telegram bot delivery, internal notify endpoint, and voice transcription helper.

out_of_scope.item: Non-Telegram authentication or account merge flows.
Automated payout execution to partners or support-managed cash-out.
Destructive schema migration strategy or release-management automation.
Full regression sign-off for this documentation-only wave.
Replacing the current JSON block report format or renderer contract.

use_case.summary: Authenticate from Telegram, ensure a stable User record keyed by telegram_id, and persist birth/profile fields needed by downstream report flows.
use_case.scenario: Valid initData or explicit development bypass resolves one User and returns the current profile payload.
User supplies name, date, place, optional time and location metadata; saved profile becomes the source for B2C report creation.

use_case.summary: Create a report from the logged-in user's stored profile, consuming subscription/quota or credits when required.
use_case.scenario: Entitled user creates natal, forecast, solar, synastry, or horary report and receives report_id/client_id immediately.
Horary uses subscriber weekly quota first, then CRD credits; blocked users receive an explicit paywall error.

use_case.summary: Generate report sections asynchronously, persist ordered chunks, allow full or partial regeneration, and expose readable report state.
use_case.entrypoints: POST /api/workflows/report/async; POST /api/workflows/report; POST /api/admin/reports/{id}/regenerate/async; POST /api/admin/reports/{id}/sections/{section}/regenerate/async; GET /api/reports/{id}; GET /api/admin/reports/{id}
use_case.scenario: Workflow initializes run and chunks, computes chart data, generates sections, and marks report completed or failed with evidence.
Admin or user retries a failed report or one section without breaking report ownership and chunk ordering.

Completed `week_forecast` detail payloads expose a canonical WeekBrief product surface; `/week` renders honest empty/in_progress/error states when canonical Week data is absent, while deep-read chunks remain a secondary report-reading layer rather than a substitute overview.

use_case.summary: Initiate payment, persist checkout session when enabled, receive webhook confirmation, and mutate subscriptions, horary credits, or one-off report unlocks exactly once.
use_case.scenario: Successful subscription payment writes a Transaction, updates Subscription, and extends subscription_active_until.
Successful horary pack payment writes a payment Transaction and a CRD top-up Transaction.

One-off report payment persists checkout session, grants exactly one unlock, and lets the flagged natal_master, month_forecast, year_forecast, or solar_return flow continue from /billing/complete back into /create or /read without losing access state.

use_case.summary: Resolve referral codes on signup and reward either trial days or partner revenue share without duplicate linkage.
use_case.entrypoints: Telegram start_param; bot /start referral arg; referral share pages; billing webhook callback into partner reward logic
use_case.scenario: One referee can be linked to one referrer exactly once; signup reward is applied according to intended referral policy.
When a referred payer completes payment and the referrer is a partner, commission is credited to partner balance.

use_case.summary: Return a compact daily feed from calculated transit facts and an optional low-cost LLM interpretation layer.
use_case.scenario: Frontend loads the feed payload with date, moon sign, moon phase, vibe text, and traffic-light summary.

Feed endpoint emits a canonical DayBrief DTO (`day_brief_canon_v1`) with hero, four domain cards, premium state, CTA, and explicit per-domain statuses; each domain owns `score`, human `description`, personalized `why_astro_text`, and field-level status, while legacy Day windows/actions/risks/explainability are not primary contract fields.

use_case.summary: Inspect reports, users, clients, tickets, analytics, audit logs, health, and trigger regeneration or diagnostics.
use_case.scenario: Admin can inspect report metadata, chunks, runs, and trigger regeneration flows.
Admin can trigger the diagnostics runner and collect log-driven evidence for core pipeline health.

use_case.summary: Send Telegram notifications for completed reports and support bot-native signup/referral or voice-related operator tasks.
use_case.entrypoints: bot polling handlers; POST bot /notify; faster-whisper transcription
use_case.scenario: Backend sends an internal notify request and the bot either delivers it or returns a non-fatal blocked/not-found status.
Voice media can be transcribed locally for bot task flows without changing report-generation contracts.

business_invariants.invariant: Telegram identity is canonical; telegram_id is the durable user key across backend, frontend, and bot flows.
Engine-first policy holds: calculation facts come from StelliumEngine and related helpers; LLM layers interpret provided facts and must return JSON blocks.
Typed JSON boundaries are mandatory for API payloads, report sections, and frontend/backend exchange.
Access control is checked before starting report generation; unauthorized creation must return an explicit business error, not a silent no-op.

One-off unlocks are granted on payment success, exposed through /api/users/me.report_unlocks together with /api/users/me.report_access, and consumed only on successful report creation; admin report gifts use the same entitlement-first consume path, and read access after creation remains ownership-based.
Async report execution persists ReportRun and ordered ReportChunk state before report completion is exposed.
Admin-only endpoints require admin authorization via the Telegram-auth path.
Intended referral behavior from current business docs is 15 days to referee and 15 days to regular referrer, or 20 percent partner commission; implementation drift is a defect, not a scope cut.
Stored referral_code is intended to be used as-is in web links according to docs/WORKFLOW.md; backward-compatible resolvers may accept legacy prefixes.
Notification failures must not roll back already completed report generation or billing persistence.

expected_failure_handling.policy: Invalid or expired Telegram auth yields 401; valid development bypass is limited to development mode.
Incomplete profile yields 400; missing entitlement yields 402 with explicit guidance to subscribe or buy credits.
LLM provider or validation failures may degrade to per-section fallback content; hard failure occurs if usable section count falls below the workflow threshold.
Webhook payloads with missing or invalid user identifiers are logged and ignored instead of mutating random records.
Pending checkout sessions may require polling; if the user returns later, the unlock must still be visible and reusable until successful create consumes it.
Self-referral and duplicate referral links are ignored; reward logic must remain idempotent.
Feed generation should return a safe fallback vibe text when LLM generation fails.
Blocked chat or chat_not_found is treated as a contained delivery failure and does not fail the originating business transaction.
Diagnostics should surface failed steps with block-oriented log evidence rather than partial silent success.

known_defects.defect: Business docs promise 15-day referral rewards and as-is referral links, while current backend and bot constants use 14 days and current frontend share/profile pages prepend ref_ to referral_code. Intended behavior and implementation are misaligned.

backend/app/services/feed_service.py treats client.generate(...) as a string even though current LLM clients return (content, usage). Non-stub feed modes fall into fallback handling instead of using live LLM output.
Shared artifacts still describe legacy Day windows/actions/risks/explainability and compatibility semantics even though the intended Day product is now canonical hero + 4 domains + CTA only.
backend/app/diagnostics.py references assemble_markdown and ReportSection symbols that are not imported in the current snapshot, so /api/diagnostics/run cannot provide full green evidence.

Some server-side admin pages/actions fetch protected admin endpoints without Telegram auth, or with hardcoded X-Telegram-Auth: 123456789, which only works under development bypass assumptions and is not production-safe.

knowledge_graph.rule: requirements.xml is the canonical source of truth for all UC/SCN/DEF identifiers; graph views in markdown or XML must only reference IDs declared here.

success_criteria.criterion: A valid Telegram user can round-trip profile data and subsequently satisfy report-creation prerequisites.
An entitled user receives report_id/client_id immediately, and the resulting report reaches completed or explicitly failed/fallback state with persisted chunks.
Async runs preserve report, chunk, and run state transitions with traceable report_id and section_id evidence.

A successful payment produces the correct Transaction plus subscription or credit mutation or one active report unlock exactly once; the flagged natal_master, month_forecast, year_forecast, and solar_return bridge can continue from /billing/complete to /read/{id} with access_source=report_entitlement, while /api/users/me exposes both unlock counts and per-report access truth.

Admin surfaces can inspect and mutate operational objects only through authorized paths with visible evidence, and one-off report gifts use entitlement-first grant/consume semantics with canonical report-type normalization.
A referral link produces at most one referral edge per referee and applies the intended reward path.
Feed endpoint returns the documented response shape and a user-readable vibe, even under degraded mode.
Notification requests are deliverable or safely contained without corrupting report or billing state.
